brief.subject: Poor credit is pushing car insurance costs up sharply
brief.headline: Drivers with poor credit see auto insurance premiums climb nearly 38%
brief.dek: Auto insurance costs keep rising for drivers with weak credit, and the FTC adds new details in its pricing case against Amazon.
brief.lede: Drivers with poor credit have seen auto insurance premiums rise nearly 38% over three years. That makes your credit score a real factor in a major monthly bill.

sections.heading: Weak credit, pricier car insurance
bullets: Premiums for drivers with poor credit are up nearly 38% over the past three years, according to NerdWallet's 2026 rates report.
Many insurers factor credit into pricing, so a low score can quietly raise your renewal bill.
Check your renewal notice against last year's to spot how much your premium has moved.

sections.heading: FTC unseals more in Amazon case
bullets: The FTC and 22 states filed an updated complaint against Amazon with previously redacted details.
Regulators allege Amazon secretly manipulated its search-ad auctions to inflate prices and hit financial targets.
The claims are allegations for now; the case shows regulators are still pursuing hidden pricing tactics.

items.title: New Details Emerge in Amazon Ads Auction-Rigging Case
